answer: Each identity posts its own bond, and vote weight counts only stake locked across many rounds. Faking thousands of agents means thousands of deposits plus foregone yield. New identities start at zero weight, so the wharf of real participation is never free. Since each fake seat pays rent while honest votes are scarce, Sybil farming loses money once marginal cost per identity exceeds one vote's value. Honest agents raise that price, and the spiral of larger deposits makes each fake seat dearer than the last. The prism of stake, time and work splits a wallet into claims never counted twice.
